RAJYA SABHA
————
List of Questions for WRITTEN ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the August 2, 2002/Sravana 11, 1924 (Saka)
————
(Ministries :  Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Environment and Forests;
Food Processing Industries; Human Resource Development; Ocean
Development; Railways; Science and Technology; Steel;
Youth Affairs and Sports)
Total number of questions—155
390
Crop loss due to Monsoon failure
1761. DR. ABRAR AHMED: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether the dry spell in Northern
India sparks fears of drought;
(b) whether Government are aware that
Kharif crops like maize, groundnut, and a
few varieties of Bajra can not be sown, if
there are no rains resulting in crop losses to
the tune of Rs. 1200 crores; and
(c) if so, how Government propose to
meet the situation?
Projects to forecast crop production
1762. MISS MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) what is the status of Government's
project of forecasting crop production
through satellite studies and land-based
observations, FASAL;
(b) the reasons for the delay in the take
off;
(c) by when these projects would really
take off; and
(d) how the project would help the small
and marginal farmers?
Replacing vessels of Fisheries Survey
of India
†1763. SHRI RAMACHANDRA
KHUNTIA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) the total number of vessels available
with Fisheries Survey of India and the details
of amount spent on their repairs during the
last three years, year-wise;
(b) whether Government propose to
declare these vessels as unusable and to
purchase new vessels in their place;
(c) if so, by when new vessels are likely
to be purchased; and
(d) if not, the reasons therefor?
Exploitation of water resources
†1764. SHRI JHUMUK LAL
BHENDIA: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that as a result of

MSP of arecanut
1765. SHRI K.B. KRISHNA
MURTHY:
DR. VIJAY MALLYA:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that arecanut
farmers in Karnataka are saddled with huge
unsold stocks of the crop due to steep fall in
prices;
(b) whether it is also a fact that there is
no market intervention by Central agencies
like NAFED in that State;
(c) whether Karnataka Government
concerned with the plight of farmers, have
proposed to the Centre for procurement of
arecanut at a minimum support price of
Rs. 65/- per kg; and
(d) whether Government have
considered the request favourable; if so, the
amount per kg. of arecanut fixed by
Government?
Remunerative price for cotton growers
1766. SHRI BACHANI LEKHRAJ:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether cotton growers of various
States, including Gujarat are not getting
remunerative price for their crop and a large
number of farmers are reported to have
committed suicide;
(b) if so, the number of such cases during
the last two years; and
(c) the remedial measures taken by
Government in this regard?
Subsidy to M.P. for Kharif crops
†1767. SHRI SURESH PACHOURI:
Will the Minister of AGRICULTURE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether drought affected areas in
Madhya Pradesh have been determined on
the basis of anawari of kharif crops as per
the scarcity manual; if so, whether rabi crops
have also been affected in other districts
due to decrease in the area cultivation of
rabi crop, low rain fall and non-availability
of water on time;
(b) whether Government are formulating
any scheme to provide benefit of input
subsidy and other grant-in-aid to the State
for the affected areas of rabi crop, besides
drought affected areas; and
(c) if so, by when, the input subsidy
would be provided to the State?
Insurance claims of farmers in Andhra
Pradesh
1768. SHRI RAMA MUNI REDDY
SIRIGIREDDY: Will the Minister of
AGRICULTURE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that insurance
claims of more than 8,000 farmers from
Adilabad District of Andhra Pradesh, for
damage to cotton crop, have not been settled;
(b) if so, the reasons for the delay in
settling their claims; and
